title: A one-dimensional local domain with principal maximal ideal is regular
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local domain of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. If $\mathfrak m=\pi A$ for some nonzero $\pi\in A$, then $A$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr, line 29104), condition (4) implies the regular-local assertion in condition (3) when dimension one is given

proof.text: Rewrite the maximal ideal as the span of the nonzero element π. Mathlib Submodule.spanFinrank_singleton hπ gives its spanFinrank equal to 1. Rewrite ringKrullDim A using hdim. The two ranks are therefore equal, and Mathlib isRegularLocalRing_iff A yields regularity by the regular-local definition [def-weil-regular-scheme].
